title: Central content sectors are isomorphic to cyclic type-A cyclotomic KLR algebras
statement: Over any field F in the charged finite-e conventions, the explicit maps ρ:R^Λ_α→H^Λ_α and σ:H^Λ_α→R^Λ_α from the preceding forward and inverse relation lemmas are mutually inverse, for every content α, including zero sectors. Here H^Λ_α is only the central CRT content sector; no primitivity is assumed. Thus H^Λ_α=0 iff R^Λ_α=0, and summing over finite height-d contents gives H^Λ_d≅⊕_α R^Λ_α. On idempotents the maps are literal identity, and the dot image is x_r−i_r (DG) or 1−q_H^(−i_r)X_r (NG). This result precedes the late dimension/basis and primitive-block theorems. No algebraic closure hypothesis is required.
strategy: The two declared relation lemmas construct the maps over F from finite nilpotent evaluations of explicit invertible-constant source series. The CRT spectrum splits over the actual c_i, not an algebraic closure. In R the inverse polynomial generators have exactly the eigenword projectors e(ν), because nilpotent dots shift those distinct scalar eigenvalues; their regular-module CRT projectors therefore are e(ν), with zero on other contents. Hence σ(e_α)=1_R and σ annihilates every other central sector. The restriction is unital. For generator composites, σρ(y_r)=y_r and ρσ(z_r)=z_r by the finite sum of projectors. On crossings, σ(Φ_r Q_r^(-1)e(ν))=(ψ_r Q_r−P_r+P_r)Q_r^(-1)e(ν)=ψ_r e(ν); the reverse composite sends ψ_r Q_r−P_r to Φ_r−P_r=T_r (or s_r), on each word. These are literal ordered expressions, not a commutation of ψ with its coefficient. Thus the composites fix all presentation generators and are identity. If H_α=0, the already constructed σ satisfies σ(e_α)=1_R, forcing1_R=0; conversely the forward inverse identities force H_α=0 if R_α=0. Zero rings and rankzero are therefore included without a nonzero-block premise. Neither exact dimension nor primitive terminology has entered this proof. The full source color-case verifications and the completed all-equal eight-term calculation reside in the declared preceding local relation lemmas.
